original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.

actual_scope: Two rank-at-most-q matrices in one paired-star internal gap, each with P_s Z P_f = 0: can every helped core block of their sum have rank 2q? Start from two copies of the rank-q witness on complementary coordinates.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks whether a changed query demand or caller removes work. This package does not change a caller or a supplier bill. It answers open question 1 of open PR #7053, a rank question on the one-gap paired-star schedule already in that card's predecessor line (#5747, #7025, #7053).
bottleneck_link: Side result, not a supplier invoice. The selected signed bill and kappa are unchanged. The calculation prices one internal gap of the paired-star schedule and does not claim a paid-profile improvement.
stop_rule: Stop after the complementary-copy test and either an explicit pair whose three blocks have rank 2q or a proof that no such pair exists under the stated square equation. Do not search words, retake the one-map theorem, or move to an every-stage schedule.
evidence: Proof in PROOF.md over any characteristic-2 field. verify.py checks the identity pair, the singular image cap, the failed complementary copies, the parity tuples, and an exhaustive q=1 census. No new kappa.

open_questions.question: At an odd stage, can external gaps of total rank q(g-3), together with the two exhibited maps, meet A_j + B_j = I_d on every leaf at g=31, q=26?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The inequality system is feasible at 728, which is the #7025 count. A block solution would show that two maps can return the external equations to that count at odd stages. It would still not be a word.
open_questions.first_step: At stage t=1, place the two maps, set the three helped external blocks to zero, and test the cover in PROOF.md on the remaining leaves.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not rebuild the monomial transport. A passing rank tuple is not a word. This is not the one-matrix gap tuple of #7053 and not the every-stage question.

open_questions.question: For 0 < rank(B21) < q, can two rank-at-most-q maps attain next-block rank q+rank(B21) and own-block rank 2q at the same time?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The image cap is proved for every off-diagonal block. The extremes rank 0 and rank q are attained. Intermediate ranks would price every legal half rather than only the singular and invertible cases.
open_questions.first_step: At q=4, take B21 of rank 1 and B12 = I_4, and test whether a sum of two rank-at-most-4 maps meets both ranks while killing im P_f.
open_questions.blocked_by: The identity witness uses B21 = I_q. A singular slot changes im P_f, so those functionals need not remain admissible.
